cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg22.txt <<'EOF'
test(runtime): every helper must return on the stack it was entered with

`stream_filter_register` released its frame twice and returned to garbage. That was the SECOND
defect of this shape here, and neither was findable by reading the emitter: each exit is correct in
isolation, and what is wrong is the relationship between them. So it gets a gate rather than only a
fix.

The property needs no understanding of what a helper computes. Walk its control-flow graph carrying
one number — the signed distance sp has moved since entry — and check that every `ret` sees zero.
1039 helpers on AArch64, 1041 on x86_64, both emitted with every feature on.

Run against the pre-fix emitter it reports, without executing anything:

    AArch64 __rt_stream_filter_register: `ret` with sp+48
    X86_64  __rt_stream_filter_register: `ret` with sp+56

Three things the walk had to be taught, each of which would otherwise have been a false verdict:

  - a `.globl` label is not automatically an ENTRY. `__rt_csv_parse_buffer` carries one and is
    reached only by `b` from two helpers that have already established a 112-byte frame — it is a
    shared TAIL. Analysed as an entry it reports a `ret` that is perfectly correct. An entry is
    what something CALLS, or a global nothing branches to.
  - `jnz 1f` is a GAS local label, not an indirect branch. Reading it as one made seven regex and
    json helpers unanalysable, which would have quietly exempted them.
  - `__rt_vsprintf` pushes one 16-byte record per argument and `__rt_sprintf` pops them, so its
    stack depth is not a static property at all. Ten measurements against `php -n` — zero through
    twenty arguments, mixed types, in a loop, and with work after the call — confirmed it is
    correct before it was exempted rather than after.

What a helper does that the walk cannot read makes it UNANALYSABLE, never passing, and the
unanalysable set is pinned BY NAME with a reason for each: argument-record cleanup, fiber stack
switching, indirect trampolines, and `and rsp, -16` C-call realignment. A gate that silently skips
what it cannot model would have let both instances of this bug through, so a new name appearing
there fails the test and has to be classified deliberately.
EOF
